title: Geological Hazards: Earthquakes, Tsunamis and Volcanoes
seo_title: Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science: Geological Hazards Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_code: Earth and Environmental Science Unit 4: Earth processes and hazards
standard_text: Earthquakes, faults and seismic waves; magnitude and locating epicentres; intraplate earthquakes in Australia; tsunamis; volcano types and volcanic hazards; landslides and liquefaction; hazard, risk, monitoring and mitigation. (Senior Secondary Earth and Environmental Science, Unit 4: The changing Earth – the cause and impact of Earth hazards)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science worksheets on geological hazards: earthquakes, seismic waves, magnitude, locating epicentres, tsunamis, volcanoes, landslides and risk. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Each step of 1 in magnitude: ×10 amplitude, about ×32 energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earthquakes release stress built up at plate boundaries and inside plates; P-waves arrive first, then S-waves and destructive surface waves. The S–P lag at three stations locates the epicentre. Magnitude is logarithmic: each step of 1 means 10 times the amplitude and about 32 times the energy.

Undersea earthquakes can cause tsunamis, whose speed is about √(gd). Volcanoes range from gentle shield volcanoes to explosive stratovolcanoes with pyroclastic flows. Monitoring, building codes, warning systems and land-use planning reduce risk.

Example

Magnitude 7 vs 5: amplitude ratio?

10^(7 − 5)

Answer: 100 times

Example

S–P lag of 25 s (8 km per s). Distance?

25 × 8

Answer: 200 km

Common mistakes

  • Thinking magnitude 6 is twice as strong as magnitude 3.
  • Saying tsunamis are caused by wind.
  • Thinking Australia has no earthquakes.

faq.q: Why is the damage from an earthquake not decided by magnitude alone?
faq.a: Depth, distance from towns, soil type (soft sediments amplify shaking), building quality and time of day all matter.

faq.q: Why did the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami lead to a warning centre in Australia?
faq.a: It showed that tsunamis can cross whole oceans in hours; seismic and sea-level sensors now give warnings to the Australian coast.

items.q: Why do earthquakes happen in Australia even though it is far from plate boundaries?

items.q: An earthquake is 80 km from a seismograph. Using about 8 km per second of S–P lag, how long after the P waves do the S waves arrive?

items.e: 20 × 8 = 160 km. Three stations are needed to locate the epicentre.

items.q: Why are stratovolcanoes at subduction zones often explosive?
c: their magma is viscous and rich in gas, so pressure builds up
items.e: Mount Pinatubo and Mount St Helens erupted explosively.

items.q: Which is a way to reduce the risk of earthquake damage?

items.q: What can trigger a landslide?

items.q: What causes a tsunami?
c: a sudden movement of the sea floor, usually from a large undersea earthquake, which displaces water
items.e: Landslides and volcanoes can also cause them.

items.q: Which signs can warn that a volcano may erupt?
